Fulfilling a customer's order › Stage 3: Ship the order

Alerts proposed: Ship the order

Each is its own alert. When one fires, follow its own entry in the runbook. Thresholds, windows and whether an alert pages a person are the operators’ values, not set here.

Paid orders waiting to ship, and the oldest's age

Its entry in the runbook ›

The question it answersHow many paid orders are waiting to ship, and for how long?
What it counts

Rows in 'Paid'; age from the order's OrderStatusChangedToPaid outbox row "CreationTime"

Counted on cases.

Why it is proposeda paid order still waiting has not been shipped when the customer expects the goods, and nothing moves it but a person recording the shipment: no timer watches Paid orders and nothing in the application calls the ship endpoint (lifecycle “The order is shipped”, recovery stranded). How long a wait is too long is the operators' dispatch target, not the register's. This measure is not emitted yet; deployed as written, the alert fires on No data until it is.
Which cases its entry worksBy the state the case is in: Paid. Its runbook entry groups the cases by state and works each state's tests.
ThresholdOperator value, not set here. For each measure, the value at which the alert fires. Whether it pages a person, opens a ticket or shows on a dashboard is the operators' decision.
WindowOperator value, not set here. How long the condition must hold before it fires. What the design assumes about time: No timeout: the stock is reduced when Catalog API consumes the Paid event from queue Catalog; no clock watches the message waiting there, and the queue sets no expiry; Each post is bounded only by the standard resilience handler every HTTP client carries: each attempt 10 seconds, up to 3 retries, 30 seconds in all; the posts to all subscriptions go out together and are awaited together. No clock watches the message waiting in queue Webhooks; No timeout: a person ships the goods and records it, and nothing in the application schedules or times that act.
Age boundOperator value. The stage’s promise: proposed: none assumed by the code: nothing schedules or times shipping. The operators' dispatch target would set one
No dataIt also fires when its measure cannot be counted for longer than the window. A count that finds no events in a window is zero, not missing data. A count fails when what it is read from is down; What it counts says where that is.
Symptom, not causeIt fires on what happens to cases, not on any component’s errors. Telling causes apart is the runbook’s job.
